notes: Yakov #5227: opening an issue is decided in the flow and NOWHERE else - sometimes a message earns one and sometimes it does not, and a rigid rule here would be the wrong kind of certainty. The permissions specification already said the same on the Reception agent's Outputs row. What is NOT flexible is the RECORD: every message gets an index row on disk keyed by Message-ID, and 'no issue' must never mean 'no trace' - the same failure the scheduled-watch flow exists to prevent. Spool deletion therefore hangs on the index row, not on an issue's terminal status. The issue, when opened, carries only deterministic values and fixed fields: free text from an unauthenticated source must not land in a field every party with write can read (Yakov #5033, ruling 100). The contradiction it closes: ruling 155 said the answering run executes no flow row of its own, while the loop says every dispatch resolves a row and any:E0 turns "no row" into Failed. A row with an empty may_ask keeps ruling 155 word for word and gives the dispatch something to resolve. status_after is - because this step moves no status: the asking issue stays in Waiting until the tag comes off
